Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to file a formal complaint against XXXX XXXX from Fairway Independent Mortgage Corporation regarding unethical conduct and mismanagement of my mortgage application process. He persuaded me that this was feasible, and so I chose him as my lender. While I understood that I could occupy this property as my primary residence, I was not aware of how strict and unyielding these rules are at the time of this ill-informed decision. 

This misclassification has resulted in numerous challenges for me, including difficulties in securing other financial products and credit due to the property 's primary occupancy status. While trying to honor these loan obligations, I faced other problems moving into the unit because I inherited distressed tenants from the previous owner and had to pursue eviction proceedings for 2 of these tenants for not paying rent and refusing to leave the premises. 

If I had been properly advised to get an investment loan, I wouldnt have to move into the unit and could more easily recover financially from these losses by renting all the units out. So in addition to inheriting non-paying tenants, I also had to move into the unit as soon as possible which was extremely stressful and challenging from a legal perspective. 

In hindsight, I believe XXXX XXXX failed to conduct basic care in my application process. I have been struggling to explain to creditors and lenders why I reportedly have two primary residences. I already owned another property prior to XXXX XXXX XXXX, that was designated as my primary residence prior to this second purchase. As a result, I was guided to make another property as my primary residence without fully understanding the severity and long term negative impacts of the mortgage clause that prohibits this to the extent that I will be seen as a higher mortgage lending risk anytime I ever seek to purchase another property again. 

Additionally, XXXX XXXX recommended purchasing mortgage points without adequately explaining the long-term ramifications of this decision. I now realize that I could have easily made extra principal payments instead of buying down the interest rate, which would have been a more financially prudent choice given my other liabilities. 

The cumulative effect of these actions has caused me significant distress and financial hardship. I feel trapped and confused about the circumstances surrounding my mortgage agreement, and I believe that XXXX XXXX acted in his/her own self-interest rather than prioritizing my best interests. He should have indicated clearly that I needed an investment loan, not a primary residence loan. 

I request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau conduct a thorough investigation into this matter and take appropriate action against XXXX XXXX and Fairway Independent Mortgage Corporation if any wrongdoing is found. Additionally, I seek assistance in documenting my experience and rectifying the errors made during the mortgage application process and mitigating the financial consequences of these actions. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response and resolution of this issue. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

I am submitting this formal complaint against the sellers Carvana and XXXX regarding my auto financing contract as the debtor. After a thorough review, I have identified significant violations of federal and state laws, including the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), CFPB regulations, and Michigan state law. Below, I outline these violations in detail : Misrepresentation of Amount Financed ( 15 U.S.C. 1638 ( a ) ( 2 ) ( A ) ; 12 C.F.R. 1026.4 ) The contract included a down payment within the amount financed, which should have been disclosed as part of the finance charge, as required by TILA. Regulation Z ( 12 C.F.R. 1026.4 ) mandates that any finance charge must be clearly disclosed and separated from the amount financed to avoid misrepresentation.

Failure to Disclose Holder in Due Course ( 16 C.F.R. 433.2 ) The contract did not include a statement that Carvana, as the holder, is subject to all claims and defenses that I, as the consumer, could assert against the seller. This omission violates federal regulations designed to protect consumers from unfair practices. 

Incorrect Credit Reporting ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ) ( ii ) ) The contract is inaccurately reported to credit bureaus as an auto loan. According to CFPB guidelines, a loan and a retail installment contract are distinct, and this misclassification constitutes reporting of false or inaccurate information.

Unclear and Unitemized Fees ( 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ; 15 U.S.C. 1638 ) A {$270.00} registration fee was charged without a clear breakdown or explanation. TILA mandates clear and itemized disclosures of all fees associated with the contract, which were not provided in this instance.

Failure to Provide Right to Obtain Amount Financed ( 15 U.S.C. 1638 ( a ) ( 2 ) ( B ) ) The contract lacks a required statement informing me of my right to request an itemization of the amount financed. This omission constitutes non-compliance with TILA disclosure requirements. 

Insurance Charges Not Properly Disclosed ( 15 U.S.C. 1638 ) If insurance was a required condition of this financing agreement, it was neither included in the finance charge nor was an option provided for me to accept or waive the insurance. This violates TILA 's requirement for comprehensive and clear disclosure of loan terms.

Electronic Signature Consent Violations ( 15 U.S.C. 7001 et seq. ) I did not give explicit consent for the use of an electronic signature, nor was there a clear disclosure process explaining the terms of signing electronically. This omission violates federal electronic contract regulations that mandate transparent consent and disclosure. 

Failure to Identify the Creditor ( 15 U.S.C. 1638 ( a ) ( 1 ) ; 12 C.F.R. 1026.18 ( a ) ( 1 ) ) The contract does not clearly identify the creditor responsible for the disclosures. TILA requires that the creditor making the disclosures be properly identified, which did not occur in this agreement.

product: Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service
story:
On XX/XX/year> I received a cashiers check in the amount of {$3000.00} from a buyer I connected with on XXXX who agreed to purchase my piano for {$1000.00}. The buyer stated that the remaining funds were intended to pay movers on their behalf.

I deposited the cashiers check at First Horizon Bank ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ). At the time of deposit, I specifically asked the teller XXXX whether the check would be placed on hold. The teller responded no. I was not informed that the funds were being made available on a provisional basis or that they were subject to reversal. The full amount was posted to my account and made available the following morning. At no point did the bank explain that availability did not constitute final settlement. Based on the banks response and conduct, I reasonably believed the funds were final and could not be taken back.

Acting in good faith and under that belief, I sent {$2000.00} to the mover via XXXX transfer. The receipt is attached. 
On the evening of XX/XX/XXXX, after speaking with my father, I became aware for the first time that the transaction resembled a known scam pattern. This was the first indication that I might be at risk. At that point, I transferred the remaining {$1000.00} into my XXXX XXXX account in an effort to protect myself. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, the cashiers check was returned as fraudulent, and First Horizon debited the full amount from my account. I was not contacted or informed by the bank that the check had bounced ; I discovered this myself when checking my account. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, I visited a First Horizon branch and spoke in person with the branch manager, XXXX, and the teller XXXX who deposited the check. During this conversation, XXXX stated to me, I believe you are not part of the scam. However, he then stated that the bank would not file a fraud claim because this was considered a scam and therefore I was liable.

Approximately thirty minutes after I left the branch, XXXX called me and advised that I send the remaining {$1000.00} back to the bank. I responded that First Horizon was legally obligated to initiate a fraud claim. XXXX stated that a claim had already been filed and that this was why he was instructing me to return the funds. 
I asked for the reference number for the alleged fraud claim. XXXX refused, stating verbatim, I am not able to provide that information. I pressed him on why the reference number could not be shared, and he repeatedly instructed me to call the number on the back of my debit card, without providing documentation or confirmation.

I questioned whether the claim actually existed, noting that only thirty minutes had passed since I provided all relevant information and that it did not appear possible for a claim determination to have been made in that timeframe. XXXX insisted the claim existed but continued to refuse to provide any reference number or written confirmation.

While I understand that Regulation CC allows banks to make funds available prior to final settlement, consumers reasonably rely on employee representations when directly asking about holds and risk. In this case, the banks response, immediate availability of funds, lack of clarification that the deposit was provisional, and failure to notify me that the check had bounced led me to reasonably believe the funds were final. Once I became aware of the risk, I acted promptly and in good faith.

Despite acknowledging that I was a victim of the scam, First Horizon has treated me as liable while providing inconsistent information, failing to clearly disclose that the funds were provisional, refusing transparency regarding the alleged fraud claim, and failing to provide timely notice that the cashiers check had been returned as fraudulent.

Mismanagement of Taxes and Insurance- The borrower was on a fixed income from Social Security , and based on her financial limitations, the servicer should have set aside funds for taxes and insurance. 
Despite a {$650000.00} reverse mortgage credit line, taxes and insurance were not deducted, forcing the borrower into default. 
Upon contacting the tax assessment office, I was informed that no taxes were owed, meaning the mortgage company advanced funds and added excessive charges beyond what was necessary.

The mortgage company has sent a third-party repair company to the property without my authorization, incurring additional costs that further inflate the balance. 
These inspections, repairs, and fees were not authorized, not requested, and not needed, yet they continue to increase the estates financial burden. 
4. Lack of Communication & Refusal to Work with the Estate- I have made countless attempts to contact the mortgage servicer, only to be transferred from department to department , disconnected, and ignored. 
The attorney representing the bank refused to delay the foreclosure sale despite the pending insurance claim payout and extenuating circumstances. 
The servicer and lender are completely disregarding the medical, financial, and personal hardships of the borrower and her family.

5. Predatory & Deceptive Practices of Reverse Mortgage Servicer- This reverse mortgage preyed upon an elderly borrower, setting her up for financial hardship with no clear protections or assistance. 
The exorbitant fees, lack of transparency, and aggressive foreclosure tactics seem designed to strip families of their homes rather than provide the financial security that reverse mortgages claim to offer. 
Heirs are not being considered, despite the devastating circumstances of the borrowers passing and the total loss of the home. 
Request for Urgent CFPB Intervention Given the egregious nature of these actions, I am pleading for immediate assistance from the CFPB to : Delay or halt the foreclosure sale until a fair resolution can be reached. 
Ensure that the insurance proceeds are properly applied to the balance as outlined in the original mortgage contract. 
Investigate the excessive fees, charges, and forced-placed insurance issues that have unfairly inflated the debt. 
Hold the mortgage servicer accountable for their failure to properly communicate and work with the estate. 
Review the predatory nature of this reverse mortgage and the undue hardship it has caused both the borrower and her family. 
This has been an emotionally and financially devastating ordeal, made worse by the lack of compassion, transparency, and fairness from the mortgage company. The borrower deserved better, and as the estate administrator, I am simply trying to make things rightbut I am being met with roadblocks at every turn.

Navy Federal Credit Union ( NFCU ) is violating federal consumer protection laws by controlling my vehicle collateral ( title ) and note without legal authority and refusing to honor my contractual alternative performance rights. 

In XX/XX/year>, I obtained an {$81000.00} vehicle loan that included a promissory note instrument with an " in lieu of payment of instrument '' clause. This clause allowed me to satisfy the debt through alternative performance - providing an amended contract and perfected security interest instead of monetary payments. I properly exercised this contractual right and fulfilled all requirements. However, the lender has improperly rejected my valid alternative performance and continues to control my vehicle collateral and demand payment via cash. 

I've sent multiple notices ( Notice of Default, Opportunity to Cure, Formal Notice of Default Before Arbitration ), and called multiple times, only for NFCU and its agents to ignore ( hang up on me ) my core dispute, suggesting this was a credit reporting agency issue, which it is not. I've requested documentation as to where my promissory note was being held, again being ignored and told that specific departments don't exist ( securitization, XXXX, clearing, etc ). The lender 's agent even told me that NFCU does not follow bylaws or federal law. 

The core problem is that NFCU sold/assigned my promissory note to a trust/trust company within months of origination ( standard industry practice ), yet continues acting as if they own the debt ( the debt follows the note ). NFCU retained only servicing rights but is making material decisions about my collateral without legal authority from the current note holder. This is blocking me from transferring to my irrevocable trust. This is all still happening even after NFCU 's POA and security interest have been revoked. 

The lender has breached our contract by refusing to honor my properly exercised " in lieu of payment '' clause, and trying to maintain contractual rights of a holder in due course even though they transferred/assigned my promissory note inconspicuously. 

SPECIFIC VIOLATIONS 1. TRUTH IN LENDING ACT VIOLATIONS- Failure to provide assignment notices when my note was transferred - Misrepresentation of creditor identity - continuing to collect as if they own the debt - Failure to identify current creditor when requested 2. FAIR DEBT COLLECTION PRACTICES ACT VIOLATIONS - Collecting on debt not owned - they sold my note but continue collections - Misrepresenting legal authority - claiming rights they don't possess - Unfair practices - refusing contractual alternative performance 3. UNFAIR, DECEPTIVE, OR ABUSIVE ACTS OR PRACTICES ( UDAAP ) - Deceptive : Misrepresenting their authority over my collateral - Unfair : Denying my contractual alternative performance rights- Abusive : Leveraging my lack of understanding about securitization to maintain improper control 4. UCC ARTICLE 9 VIOLATIONS - Failure to provide proper assignment notices to the debtor - Acting without legal standing to control security interests- Improper security interest perfection ( potentially wrong method for collateral type ) 5. FINANCIAL HARM - Improper collections- All payments made after note assignment may be invalid - Blocked vehicle transfer - Can not transfer vehicle to my irrevocable trust for estate planning - Denial of contractual rights - Can not exercise valid alternative performance despite compliance - Improper lien maintenance - Vehicle title shows a lien despite my contractual compliance/performance - Legal costs - Forced to seek legal remedy for lender 's breach and regulatory violations - Opportunity costs - Estate planning delayed, potential tax implications- Credit implications- Risk of improper credit reporting on discharged obligation

I am filing this complaint to bring attention to what I believe was an unfair or misleading mortgage-servicing practice that could harm other borrowers. I wired {$140000.00} to Planet Home Lending , LLC for my mortgage loan, loan number XXXX. The wire instructions specifically stated Apply to Principal. This was intended as a principal-only curtailment, not a payoff. After the funds were sent, I was contacted and told Planet Home Lending was treating the payment as a payoff. I clarified that this was incorrect and that the payment was intended to be applied to principal only. I was then told the funds would be returned unless I paid off the remaining balance within approximately 24 hours. Because of that pressure, I sent an additional wire for {$4400.00}. Unlike the first wire, this second wire was marked Apply to Payoff. The different instructions on the two wires show the difference in intent : the first payment was principal-only, and the second payment was only sent after I was told the first payment would be returned unless I completed the payoff. The total wired was {$140000.00}. My concern is that a borrower who makes a large principal-only payment should not be forced into an all-or-nothing payoff decision under threat of having the payment returned. This type of communication could pressure borrowers into sending funds they did not intend to send, or prevent borrowers from making legitimate principal-only payments. I am not primarily seeking personal financial relief. I am filing this complaint because I believe this payment-handling practice should be reviewed so it does not happen to other borrowers. I would like Planet Home Lending to review the handling of this transaction and provide a written explanation addressing the following : 1. Why a wire clearly marked Apply to Principal was treated as a payoff ; 2. Whether Planet Home Lending allows borrowers to make large principal-only payments without paying off the full loan ; 3. The policy, servicing rule, investor requirement, or other basis Planet relied on when it threatened to return the funds unless I paid off the remaining balance ; 4. Whether my loan was current at the time the {$140000.00} principal payment was received ; 5. How Planet trains representatives to handle large principal-only payments ; 6. Whether Planet will review the call handling and communication used in this matter ; 7. What steps Planet will take to ensure borrowers who clearly designate payments as principal-only are not misclassified as payoff borrowers or pressured into sending additional funds unnecessarily. My goal is for Planet Home Lending to review this process and ensure that future borrowers are clearly informed of their options when making a principal-only payment, especially when the payment is large. A principal-only payment should not be automatically treated as a payoff when the borrowers written instructions say otherwise. Attachment 1 shows the first wire request for {$140000.00}, which was marked Apply to Principal. Attachment 2 shows the second wire request for {$4400.00}, which was marked Apply to Payoff.
